samples.summary: The switch of session/CLI cookie `secure` from `NODE_ENV` to `useSecureCookies()` has no test that distinguishes new from old behavior
samples.evidence: `auth.controller.ts:372` and `cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:58` now call `useSecureCookies()`. `useSecureCookies` itself is unit-tested in `oauth-state.spec.ts:90-127`, but every test that observes the *cookies these two call sites set* only drives the `NODE_ENV` fallback: `auth.controller.spec.ts:504-535` explicitly `delete process.env.GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` in `beforeEach` and asserts secure=true under NODE_ENV=production / false under development — assertions that hold identically against the pre-change `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` code. The same is true of `cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:196-221`. So the wiring (an https `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` with NODE_ENV=development must now yield `secure:true` on the *session* cookies, and an http callback URL under production must yield `secure:false`) is untested end to end; reverting the two call sites to `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` would leave the whole backend suite green.

No test passes `command` to any orchestrator or asserts it lands in the envelope: `grep -n "command:" packages/cli/test` returns only output.test.ts, upstream-error.test.ts, ctx.test.ts hits, and every `runFilesUpload(...)`/`runFilesDownload(...)`/`runDocsImport(...)` call in `files-upload.test.ts`, `files-download.test.ts`, `docs-import.test.ts`, `notes-import.test.ts`, `slides-import.test.ts`, `upstream-error.test.ts` omits it. So `docs import`, `notes import`, `slides import`, `files upload` and `files download` could silently emit unattributed envelopes (the exact regression the change exists to prevent) with the suite green; only `errorEnvelope`'s own unit test covers the builder.

finding.evidence: `auth.controller.ts:372` and `cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:58` now call `useSecureCookies()`. `useSecureCookies` itself is unit-tested in `oauth-state.spec.ts:90-127`, but every test that observes the *cookies these two call sites set* only drives the `NODE_ENV` fallback: `auth.controller.spec.ts:504-535` explicitly `delete process.env.GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` in `beforeEach` and asserts secure=true under NODE_ENV=production / false under development — assertions that hold identically against the pre-change `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` code. So the wiring (an https `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` with NODE_ENV=development must now yield `secure:true` on the *session* cookies, and an http callback URL under production must yield `secure:false`) is untested end to end; reverting the two call sites to `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` would leave the whole backend suite green.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. auth.controller.ts:366-376 and cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:61 now derive `secure` from useSecureCookies() (oauth-state.ts:189-207, which prefers GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL's scheme / COOKIE_SECURE over NODE_ENV). The only tests that observe cookies from those two call sites are auth.controller.spec.ts:482-550, whose beforeEach deletes GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL (line 492) so it exercises only the NODE_ENV fallback, and cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:196-221, which sets only NODE_ENV=production and never touches GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL/COOKIE_SECURE. Both assertions hold identically against the pre-change `NODE_ENV === 'production'` expression. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide greps for useSecureCookies, COOKIE_SECURE, GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL and set-cookie; the entire packages/backend/test e2e tree (no `secure`/`Set-Cookie` assertions at all — e2e specs only send wafflebase_session request cookies); no jest.mock/spy of useSecureCookies anywhere in src/auth; the enumerated list of all backend spec files; and no guard script asserting the call sites. oauth-state.spec.ts:90-127 does cover https-under-development and http-under-production, but only via useSecureCookies()/oauthStateCookieName() — the OAuth state cookie helper, not the session or CLI-confirm cookies. So reverting the two call sites would leave the suite green: a changed behavior with no test that can fail on it, which is in the test-adequacy lane.

finding.summary: The CLI consent gate's central claim — "stops an unconfirmed CLI start before GitHub" — is never asserted: passport's `canActivate` is stubbed but no test checks it wasn't called
finding.evidence: `beforeEach` (line 108-113) does `jest.spyOn(passportBase, 'canActivate').mockReturnValue(true)` but never keeps a handle on the spy, and the only `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` in the whole file is on the logger warn (line 835). The test `it('stops an unconfirmed CLI start before GitHub')` asserts `guard.canActivate(context)).toBe(true)` — which is exactly what the mocked super returns, so it holds whether or not the guard short-circuits — plus `req.__oauthState` being undefined. A regression where the guard rendered the consent page AND still fell through to `super.canActivate(context)` (redirecting the victim to GitHub with no state, the exact forced-login/CLI-phish case the gate exists for) would leave every assertion in the file green. Same for the controller-side test `'does nothing for an ordinary start (the guard already redirected)'`, which only checks `res.send` was not called.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the consent gate's central behavior — an unconfirmed CLI start is stopped before reaching GitHub — is never asserted. It is asserted, just not in the file the reviewer searched. The gate is implemented by CliLoginConfirmMiddleware, not GitHubAuthGuard: auth.module.ts:45-48 applies it to GET auth/github, and the comment at :41-43 notes middleware is the only layer that runs ahead of the guard. cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:152-160 renders the confirmation page and returns WITHOUT calling next(), so "stops before GitHub" is precisely "next not called". cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:47 asserts expect(next).not.toHaveBeenCalled() for the unconfirmed CLI start (alongside status 200 and the rendered page), and the same assertion recurs at :126, :146, :165 and :176 for mismatched confirm, port replay, challenge replay, and confirm-without-cookie. The exact regression the reviewer postulates — page rendered AND the flow still falls through toward GitHub — would call next() and turn those assertions red. Two further facts undercut the premise: (1) the quoted test names ("stops an unconfirmed CLI start before GitHub", "does nothing for an ordinary start") do not exist anywhere in the repo; the real guard test is "mints no CLI state for an unconfirmed CLI request" (github-auth.guard.spec.ts:151-156), whose assertions are non-vacuous because the mocked super returning true cannot produce the web.-prefixed __oauthState it checks; (2) the guard deliberately does NOT short-circuit an unconfirmed CLI start — github-auth.guard.ts:116-134 falls through to the web-state branch and then super.canActivate, documented at :83-86 as degrading to an ordinary browser login — so asserting super was not called there would assert behavior the code intentionally lacks.

mergedFrom.summary: No test pins the warning's interaction with an explicit COOKIE_SECURE=false on a production non-loopback http origin

finding.summary: No test covers that COOKIE_SECURE now decides `cliLoginAvailable` — the CLI consent gate on a plain-http, non-loopback origin
finding.evidence: `cliLoginAvailable` (github-auth.guard.ts:215) is `secureCookies(...) || loopbackCallback(...)`, so the new `COOKIE_SECURE` short-circuit in `secureCookies` (line 159-160) newly makes a CLI login startable on a plain-http non-loopback origin (COOKIE_SECURE=true) and newly *refuses* one on an https origin (COOKIE_SECURE=false). The existing gate tests use only `insecureConfig()`/`httpsConfig()` (spec lines 444-466, 686-700); the three new COOKIE_SECURE tests assert only `secureCookies()`'s return, `loginCookieName`, and the web state cookie's `secure` option. Nothing exercises `canActivate` with a CLI query under an overridden config, so a regression in either direction of that gate would pass green.

verdict.reason: The finding's subject does not exist in this repository. `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts` is only 182 lines (no line 215) and contains no `cliLoginAvailable`; a repo-wide grep for `cliLoginAvailable`, `secureCookies(`, and `loginCookieName` returns zero matches. The guard's CLI gate (canActivate, lines 108-135, plus assertCliStartNotCrossSite at 171-181) depends on `mode=cli`, `parseCliPort`, `req.__cliConfirmed` and `Sec-Fetch-Site` — never on cookie-security or a loopback-callback disjunction. The real helper is `isSecureCookie()`/`useSecureCookies()` in oauth-state.ts:184-207, whose only consumers are cookie names and the `secure` attribute (oauth-state.ts:61,96,145; cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:61; auth.controller.ts:373). Also, github-auth.guard.spec.ts is 268 lines, so the cited test regions (444-466, 686-700, 840) do not exist, and it has no `insecureConfig()`/`httpsConfig()` helpers or COOKIE_SECURE reference; the only COOKIE_SECURE test is oauth-state.spec.ts:109-116 (one, not three). There is therefore no behavior of the described shape that a missing test could leave unguarded.
